races.title: State Assembly, District 72
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Gracey Van Der Mark
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 72. Huntington Beach City Council member elected in 2022 and later the city's mayor, described as its first Latina mayor. Co-owns a property management business with her husband. Earlier served on a school bond oversight committee and the city Finance Commission.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed on Ballotpedia among her endorsements)
Reform California (listed on Ballotpedia among her endorsements)

cands.gaps: Her birthplace and the exact year she moved to Huntington Beach are not stated in the pages reviewed. We found no documented positions of hers on data centers or development limits, and no documented positions on property tax relief, institutional or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her city council actions are described only on her own campaign site, so we could not verify them against council records or news reporting. We found no controversies in the pages reviewed. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she grew up in an immigrant neighborhood in Los Angeles and has lived in Huntington Beach for over two decades, but it does not give her birthplace.

qual.why: Local elected office and business ownership put her in the middle range. No state-level legislative service or budget or policy career is documented in the pages reviewed. Committee and commission seats were not counted.

cands.name: Chris Kluwe
cands.bio: Former NFL punter (Seahawks, Vikings, Raiders), small businessman, high school football coach and writer. Raised in Seal Beach, UCLA graduate in history and political science. He has never held elected office. Democratic candidate for California Assembly District 72 in 2026.

controversies.text: On Feb. 18, 2025, Kluwe spoke at a Huntington Beach council meeting against a library plaque with a MAGA acrostic. He said he would engage in "peaceful civil disobedience," walked up toward council members, and police arrested and carried him out. Edison High then fired him as a coach. He said the school cited too much attention.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California and Our Revolution (as listed by Ballotpedia)
Per his Ballotpedia survey: LA/OC Building Trades, SEIU California, Operating Engineers Local 12, Climate Action California, Rep. Dave Min, Rep. Derek Tran and Sen. (Ret.) Tom Umberg

cands.gaps: We could not find Kluwe's birthplace. We found no documented stance from him on data centers, on property tax relief for homeowners, on limits on investor or foreign land buyers, on H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, on abortion, or on school vouchers or charters. He has not held public office, so there is no voting record. His campaign materials say he stands against special interests and is 'people-powered', but we found no explicit pledge to refuse any category of donor money. Wikipedia says he supports stronger regulation of Flock Safety cameras, but we could not read the original statement and did not count it. We could not confirm the nature of his small business or any outcome of the 2025 arrest.

local.label: Roots 90: He says he grew up in Seal Beach and attended local public schools and Los Alamitos High School, and his campaign says he and his wife have lived in Huntington Beach for more than two decades; his birthplace was not found.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In his Ballotpedia survey he says California has not built enough homes for decades, especially near jobs, schools and transit, and that he wants to move faster on housing by increasing supply. He says this should come without sacrificing workforce standards or decimating environmental safeguards.
